Committee responsibilities

Student Welfare Committee

Dedicated to overseeing the overall physical, academic, and socio-emotional welfare of students on campus. It provides comprehensive pastoral support, identifies student needs, and ensures access to essential campus resources, recreational avenues, and health services. The committee actively bridges communication between learners and administration to maintain an enriching, balanced collegiate journey.

College Disciplinary Committee (CDC)

Responsible for enforcing institutional discipline, ethics, and code of conduct across college blocks, hospital wards, and residential hostels. It conducts fair and transparent inquiries into reported misconduct, attendance irregularities, examination malpractice, and property damage. The committee emphasizes corrective interventions and character building while maintaining institutional dignity.

Student Mental Health & Wellness Committee (SMHWC)

A proactive body established to promote psychological well-being, mitigate academic stress, and provide timely emotional guidance to undergraduate students. Working closely with faculty mentors, institutional psychiatrists, and clinical psychologists, it conducts regular wellness workshops and screening sessions. It also facilitates confidential access to national support systems like the 24x7 TELE-MANAS helpline.

Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC)

Provides a structured, impartial, and confidential mechanism for students to lodge complaints regarding academic, administrative, or infrastructural matters. It guarantees unbiased hearings and objective fact-finding to redress grievances efficiently without fear of reprisal. The committee ensures strict compliance with regulatory standards to safeguard student rights.

Anti-Ragging Committee (ARC) & Anti-Ragging Flying Squad (ARS)

Mandated by statutory NMC and state regulations to prevent, prohibit, and eliminate ragging in all forms within and beyond the campus. The apex committee formulates preventive safeguards and investigates complaints, while the Flying Squad conducts round-the-clock physical vigil and surprise raids across hostels, dining messes, and transit zones. Any infraction is met with swift, stringent disciplinary and legal action.

College Council Committee

Serves as the apex administrative council comprising the Principal as Chairperson and all Heads of Departments as members. Meeting at least quarterly, it reviews institutional operations, student welfare, academic progress, clinical administration, and hospital services. The council ensures cohesive coordination across departments to uphold regulatory standards and educational excellence.

Curriculum Committee

Oversees the effective design, implementation, and quality assurance of the NMC Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) curriculum. It plans horizontal and vertical integration, monitors timetables, reviews internal assessment blueprints, and coordinates foundation courses, electives, and AETCOM modules. The committee regularly updates academic delivery based on feedback from departmental heads and student representatives.

Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace / Internal Complaints Committee

Constituted under the statutory provisions of the POSH Act, 2013, to ensure a secure, respectful, and gender-inclusive working and learning environment for female students, faculty, and healthcare staff. It spearheads awareness campaigns on gender equity and rights across campus. The committee conducts prompt, confidential, and empathetic inquiry into complaints, recommending stringent corrective and punitive measures.

Gender Harassment Committee

Works in synergy with institutional equity cells to promote mutual respect, non-discrimination, and gender sensitization across the campus community. It regularly conducts interactive seminars, orientation sessions, and open forums to build an environment free from gender bias. The committee handles grievances concerning gender-based discrimination with utmost discretion and sensitivity.

Hostel Advisory Committee (HAC)

Dedicated to overseeing the management, security, sanitation, and living standards across the undergraduate and postgraduate residential blocks. Comprising wardens, faculty representatives, and student nominees, it coordinates hostel maintenance, enforces curfew and visitor protocols, and monitors mess nutrition and hygiene. The committee ensures the hostels remain safe, comfortable, and conducive to academic focus.

Anti-Drug Committee (ADC)

Constituted in alignment with directives from the Telangana Anti-Narcotics Bureau (TG-NAB), KNRUHS, and district administration to eradicate substance abuse. It drives continuous awareness on the hazards of narcotics and alcohol through peer policing, guest lectures, and student pledge drives. In coordination with local law enforcement, it carries out surprise inspections and strictly penalizes violations under the NDPS Act.

Medical Education Unit (MEU)

Drives faculty development programs, basic/advanced medical education technology workshops, and modern instructional design.

Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC - Human Studies)

Operates under DHR (Department of Health Research) and CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation) approvals to ensure ethical review of all biomedical research.

Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC)

Regulates laboratory research and animal-assisted learning in compliance with CPCSEA guidelines.

Scientific & Research Advisory Committee

Promotes, evaluates, and monitors faculty, postgraduate, and student research dissertations, publications, and ICMR projects.

Hospital Infection Control Committee (HICC)

Monitors healthcare-associated infections (HAI), enforces sterilization standards, and leads antibiotic stewardship programs.

Pharmacovigilance Committee

Actively monitors, records, and reports adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to the national Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI).

Hospital Security & Safety Committee

Oversees 24x7 integrated CCTV surveillance, campus access control, emergency disaster preparedness, and fire safety protocols.

Mortality & Death Audit Committee

Conducts regular clinical audits and death review meetings to ensure high clinical care standards and diagnostic accuracy.

Medical, dental and nursing education.
